A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ConsistentChat work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison, including matching content across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original fine-tuning experiments, benchmark evaluations, consistency-stratified training experiments, and generated-dataset analyses in Sections 2 and 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains those original empirical results and additionally reports human–judge correlations and detailed corpus statistics.

M1.justification: The nine intent skeletons, query generation, CoT-assisted full-sequence response generation, and supervised fine-tuning objective remain unchanged. Appendix C retains the same generation prompts; expanded descriptions do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Training corpora, LIGHT, TOPDIAL, the three MT-EVAL tasks, and the seven commonsense/code benchmarks are retained. Human validation samples existing LIGHT/TOPDIAL settings, while the new corpus statistics describe the existing nine intent categories.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain ShareGPT, ChatAlpaca, UltraChat, LmsysChat, and the same base/instruction-tuned models. Appendix comparisons and case-study comparators also match. Newly cited evaluation methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 and Appendix A.4 add a human-evaluation protocol: three annotators rate 50 LIGHT dialogues and 50 TOPDIAL dialogues on a 1–10 scale, covering 350 and 300 responses respectively. Existing benchmark splits and training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds an analysis testing automatic consistency ratings against human judgments and descriptive analysis of corpus balance and lengths. Existing consistency, dialogue-depth, diversity, and qualitative case analyses are retained; reordered cases are not new experiments.

E5.justification: V2 introduces Pearson and Spearman correlation estimation between averaged human ratings and Qwen-2.5-72B-Instruct ratings (Table 4, Appendix A.4). Neither version reports confidence intervals, significance tests, or repeated-run/seed variability for the benchmark results.

E6.justification: V2 Table 4 adds LIGHT/TOPDIAL Pearson correlations of 0.73/0.69 and Spearman correlations of 0.70/0.66. Figures 19–20 add per-intent corpus counts and length statistics. Matched benchmark tables and case-study scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 corrects the formal generation context: v1 includes the response r_t that is supposed to be generated, whereas v2 ends with the current query q_t. The generation equations and training loss otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The main claims about intent-guided synthesis, improved consistency, and stronger conversational capabilities remain, including the abstract's headline improvement claims. Distinguishing the ConsistentChat dataset from its generating framework clarifies terminology without changing contribution scope.

C2.justification: V2 interprets human correlations as supporting evaluator reliability and new corpus statistics as demonstrating balanced coverage. The retained MT-EVAL case caption drops its comparison with all other baselines. The stated limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds a repository link described as providing code, models, and data, and discloses the ShareGPT scoring prompt and high/low thresholds of 8–10/4–6. These supplement existing generation prompts, hyperparameters, and inference templates without establishing changes to the underlying experiments.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations and brief discussion covering persona consistency, Self-Synthesized Rehearsal, FaithfulRAG, recent synthetic-data work, and human-aligned evaluation. The central positioning around intent-guided dialogue synthesis remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 clarifies consistency and dataset/framework terminology, edits explanatory paragraphs, adds 'Multi-Turn' to the title, and introduces human-evaluation subsections and acknowledgements. Appendix examples are regrouped, while the overall narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds the correlation table, ShareGPT scoring-prompt figure, and two corpus-statistics figures. Existing plots and comparison-table structures are retained. Appendix prompts and cases are relocated, and the ConsistentChat refinement-case caption correctly identifies MT-EVAL instead of TOPDIAL.

improvement.justification: Human validation supplies direct support for automatic ratings that v1 lacked, while disclosed filtering rules, corpus statistics, and resource-access information improve transparency. The validation remains limited to 50 dialogues per benchmark without inter-annotator agreement or confidence intervals, so evaluator-reliability concerns are only partly addressed. These are useful, bounded improvements.
